items.title: Find My AI Chips: the US Plans to Track GPUs Abroad - IEEE Spectrum
items.summary: To deduce an AI chip’s location, PLV measures the time it takes for a ping to travel from the chip to multiple trusted “landmark” servers around the world and back. Kyle Miller, a senior research analyst at CSET and coauthor of the report, says that for new AI chips, manufacturers could integrate PLV functionality into the hardware itself, while a firmware update could be applied to chips already in circulation. [...] Not all AI chips should be tracked, the researchers note. “The priority should be for the highest-end data center chips—the cream of the crop in high-end data center GPUs,” says Jacob Feldgoise, a senior data research analyst at CSET and coauthor of the report. [...] Whether or not a “Find My” for AI chips becomes a regulatory requirement, Feldgoise envisions tighter conditions for the export of advanced AI chips. “This is based on the increasing importance of compute to national and economic security,” he says. “The chips that generate compute are being seen as a strategic resource, so I would be unsurprised if the due diligence requirements on these devices increase as time passes.”

items.title: Google's chip business is on a faster track than Nvidia's own AI boom
items.summary:
Google introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs — its homegrown AI chips — on Monday. The TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max join the 8t and 8i it unveiled in April, the first time Google has introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Both new chips ship next year. [...] Think of it as a chip menu. The 8tx keeps data encrypted for governments, banks, and other regulated businesses, paired with processors from AMD (AMD). The 8i Max squeezes two chips into one package for requests with long context windows — the amount of information an AI model can juggle at once. [...] Google is selling on price. SemiAnalysis found that Google's current Ironwood TPU delivers up to nearly three times as much AI output per dollar as Nvidia's Blackwell chips when running AI agents, though Nvidia's top system still wins when speed is everything.

items.title: Boston Dynamics Launches Next Generation Stretch Robot | Boston Dynamics
items.summary: Boston Dynamics is the global leader in AI-enabled mobile robots that tackle the toughest industrial and safety challenges. Our robots are equipped with advanced mobility, dexterity and intelligence, enabling automation in unstructured, unsafe or hard-to-traverse spaces. We have three robots in our portfolio: Spot®, a quadruped that conducts industrial inspections, manages facility performance data and keeps people out of harm’s way; Stretch®, a box-moving robot for logistics and retail [...] As a first mover in the robotic unloading space, Stretch is the market leader and has more deployments than any competitive product in the logistics industry. The team analyzed data from more than 100,000 operating hours and tens of millions of boxes that Stretch has already unloaded to target the most common causes of unplanned downtime. The result is a robot hardened for durability and an updated modular design that enables “plug and play” part swaps for easier maintenance and serviceability. [...] The new robot also runs on a redesigned onboard computing platform that is constantly improving. Regular software releases bring gains in case detection, motion planning, pick strategies and world modeling across an entire fleet, with no hardware changes required.

items.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
items.summary: With all the human support they need, the robots are closer to radio-controlled cars than Waymos. Many tasks, such as making the bed and folding laundry, require what’s called kinematic guidance: The human pilot performs the necessary motions, and sensors transmit those movements to the robot, which copies them. These kinematically guided tasks produce especially valuable training data. Tau’s AI models might not have solved laundry folding yet, but learning from the examples of robots that have [...] But the robots are physically capable of cleaning, and they’re undeniably cute. Tau has armed each four-and-a-half-foot-tall robot with a 3D-printed “head” with antennae that allow it to communicate with Tau’s headquarters, as well as two 3D-printed claw “hands” (the more humanlike alternatives apparently aren’t durable enough, and claws do surprisingly well for most cleaning tasks). Mine was wearing a Tau Robotics shirt, and grippy socks so that it didn’t scratch hardwood floors. [...] the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants. Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.

items.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory | MIT News | Massachusetts Institute of Technology
items.summary:
But the robot sometimes sees objects only partially or from far away, or its camera might capture blurry or poorly lit images. In these cases, DAAAM might describe these objects incorrectly, such as by mistaking a gray chimney for a squirrel perched on a rooftop.

“With no way to correct itself, this wrong memory would persist as the robot proceeds in its environment, which could impact downstream applications,” Zhang says. [...] UQ-DAAAM integrates uncertainty quantification into the DAAAM framework. It allows the robot to measure its confidence in the accuracy of object descriptions and fix incorrect captions as it travels through an environment.

While on the move, the robot constantly collects and stores images of the world around it. Many of these images show the same objects captured from different angles. UQ-DAAAM uses these additional viewpoints to identify and correct unreliable descriptions. [...] “Performing this uncertainty quantification procedure across the entire map the robot generates allows it to improve its understanding of what it has observed,” Gorlo says.

Next, the researchers want to use UQ-DAAAM to guide different types of robots, like mobile robotic manipulators, and apply their uncertainty quantification techniques to other domains.

items.title: Make a Robot Arm Feel Weightless with NVIDIA Holoscan 5 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
items.summary: Picture guiding a robot arm by hand while its motors supply just enough torque to support its weight and keep the robot upright. This simple interaction, a useful starting point for robots that learn by demonstration, manipulate objects, or work alongside people, depends on a gravity-compensation loop. [...] This tutorial is built around the Seeed Studio reBot Arm B601-DM, which is an accessible, affordable platform for getting started with modern robotics control. Most low-cost robot arm development platforms use highly-geared hobby servos, which are only suitable for positional control. The reBot Arm uses quasi-direct-drive (QDD) actuators that provide high torque bandwidth for both control and sensing — important for haptic, co-bot, or other torque-oriented projects like this one.
